correctness.rationale: PASS: RESULT.md constructs four realizable cyclic templates for all n=2^k factors, computes their weights, proves outer-layer injectivity via T_{s+1}=T_s+nV_s-r and gcd(n,r)=1, and equates paired q-sets by reverse-complement symmetry. For balanced templates it proves a complete signed-prefix range [-1,k-1] using even/odd interleaving and evaluates the base moment by induction. The formula q=T-r(r+1)/2 correctly converts the moment to scattered 01 count; binomial equivalence on binary length-n words is characterized by (r,q). A genuinely separate literal-prefix and template implementation matched the exact spectra for k=2..8, yielding totals 11,20,37,70,135,264,521. The unrestricted claim follows from the template/induction argument, not those finite checks.

value.rationale: PASS: Binary paperfolding is a classical Toeplitz/automatic sequence with established ordinary and Abelian complexity. Resolving the next ordered-scattered-pair invariant at a complete unbounded family of natural dyadic lengths is a motivated refinement, and the collapse of the balanced layer to k+1 arithmetically spaced values versus n outer values is structural, not merely an isolated count.

final_claim: For each k>=2, with n=2^k, the 2-binomial factor-profile set of the standard regular paperfolding word has n distinct profiles in each of r=n/2-1 and r=n/2+1 (with identical scattered-01 values), and k+1 profiles at r=n/2 with q=n(n-2k)/8+(n/2)j, 0<=j<=k; total 2n+k+1.
limitations: No arbitrary factor length formula, order-3 or higher binomial equivalence, nor arbitrary instruction paperfolding; finite k checks supplement the all-k induction.
residual_risks: A differently named paperfolding scattered-subsequence/Parikh-matrix theorem could imply the exact dyadic spectrum.
The result is restricted to dyadic lengths k>=2 and order-2 binomial equivalence; no arbitrary-length generalization.
